timing.text: How does a server actually remember you?
Without JSON Web Tokens, any anonymous stranger could rewrite a secure database.
Take an online auction app where you tap a button to place a $62,500 bid on a rare phone.
When your app sends that bid command, the backend server instantly rejects it with an unauthorized error.
Because backend servers are forgetful, they cannot inherently trust an anonymous command.
To fix this, you first have to prove your identity by sending your login credentials to the server.
Once verified, the server creates a secure encrypted digital badge exclusively for you.
This cryptographic ID card is called a JSON Web Token.
The server sends this token back to your app, which quietly stores that text string in the background.
Now, when you try to place that massive bid again, your app automatically bundles this stored token alongside the new request before firing it off.
The server intercepts the incoming bid, inspects the attached token, and instantly verifies your identity.
With your identity securely confirmed, the endpoint finally unlocks.
And that $62,500 bid is accepted and recorded in the database,
because the system now securely knows exactly who placed it.
